extraction.segment_function: defining the fundamental conditions of human action and speech, specifically human plurality (equality and distinction), uniqueness, and natality as the capacity for new beginnings.

claims.claim: Human plurality is the basic condition of both action and speech, possessing a twofold character of equality and distinction.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Human plurality, the basic condition of both action and speech, has the twofold character of equality and distinction.

claims.claim: Speech and action reveal unique human distinctness, serving as the modes in which human beings appear to each other qua men rather than as physical objects.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Speech and action reveal this unique distinctness. Through them, men distinguish themselves instead of being merely distinct; they are the modes in which human beings appear to each other, not indeed as physical objects, but qua men.

definitions.definition: The basic condition of both action and speech, characterized by a twofold nature of equality and distinction.
In its most general sense, to take an initiative, to begin, to set something into motion.

distinctions.distinction: Human distinctness transforms the otherness shared with everything that is and the distinctness shared with everything alive into uniqueness.

must_not_be_lost: Human plurality entails both equality and distinction.
In man, otherness and distinctness become uniqueness.
To act means to take an initiative or begin something new by virtue of birth (natality).
